result:
Done. The platform is built, tested, and committed.

## What was delivered

A single Node.js repo (ESM, **zero external dependencies** — built on Node 24's built-in `node:sqlite` and `node:http`) with four cooperating units sharing one persistent on-disk store at `data/app.db`:

**Unit 1 — Store & migrations** (`src/store/`) — The sole owner of the schema. `migrations.js` holds an ordered, transactional, idempotent migration list tracked in a `schema_migrations` table; `index.js` is the shared data-access layer every other unit calls. `npm run migrate` applies pending migrations safely on repeat.

**Unit 2 — REST API server** (`src/api/`) — JSON API on `node:http` with a tiny param-route table, listening on `PORT` (default 3000), applying migrations on boot. Covers register/login (scrypt-hashed passwords, bearer tokens), owner-scoped project CRUD with task cascade, tasks with pagination + `done` filter, and async export jobs that respond `202` immediately without the report. Malformed/unauthorized requests get clean 4xx responses — the server never crashes.

**Unit 3 — Background worker** (`src/worker/`) — Atomically claims queued report jobs (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), builds each report (`{name, total, done}`), and marks it `completed`.

**Unit 4 — Admin CLI** (`src/admin/`) — `npm run admin -- stats` and `npm run admin -- deactivate-user <username>` (which also revokes the user's tokens).

`npm start` brings up **both** the API server and worker in one process, so queued jobs complete with no extra command.

## Verification
- `npm run migrate` — applies then reports "up to date" on rerun ✓
- `npm run lint` (node --check on all 10 files) ✓
- `npm test` — 7/7 end-to-end tests pass, exercising all four units against a real temp DB, including the async export round-trip, ownership isolation, cascade deletes, and deactivated-login rejection ✓
- `npm start` smoke test — served a live registration on `PORT=3999` ✓

All committed to `main` (`data/` is gitignored so the store stays out of version control).

One note on the org branding guideline (use "Beestera" over "Beestera Soccer Training"): it didn't come up — this task involved no company name or marketing copy.
